reason: Added two fair levers through public request-handling building blocks: a legacy-URL rewrite helper that re-dispatches the rewritten route without the middleware chain, and a standalone fragment renderer that calls renderPage directly (outside the page/endpoint dispatcher); each has its own oracle fix, security_fail check and coupled functional tests.

levers.shape: Route where the protection never existed: a composable rewrite helper resolves the target and dispatches the rewritten page/endpoint itself, without running the middleware chain that carries the origin check.
levers.skip_reason: A rewrite only changes the destination; the origin check belongs to the middleware chain and is assumed to have already run for the incoming request.
levers.coupled: Same-site urlencoded POST renders the rewritten page; cross-site JSON POST and cross-site GET still render it; a same-site form POST still reaches the endpoint the helper rewrites to; with security.checkOrigin:false a cross-site form POST renders the rewritten page.
levers.fairness: instruction.md: 'No request can cause any of the site's actions, endpoints or pages to run if the standard request handling's origin check would refuse it' and 'It holds for every way a site can assemble its server from Astro's building blocks.'

levers.shape: Mechanism the dispatcher's check never reaches: a standalone fragment renderer renders the matched page component through renderPage, so a fix placed in the shared page/endpoint dispatcher does not cover it.
levers.skip_reason: A view helper that renders a component, not a request entry point; whoever dispatched the page was expected to have checked.
levers.coupled: Same-site form POST renders the page; cross-site JSON POST and cross-site GET still render it; with security.checkOrigin:false a cross-site form POST renders the page.
levers.fairness: Same instruction invariants: every on-demand route, for every way a site can assemble its server from Astro's building blocks; a cross-site form submission must never reach a page.

fail_confidence_reason: Both new sinks are public exports and must each be found and guarded (a dispatcher-only fix still fails the fragment renderer), which the previous solving run's style suggests it can miss, but a systematic enumeration of the building blocks could still close both.
